version: arXiv:2310.08424v2; manuscript dated June 2024; 38 PDF pages

read_ranges.scope: entire paper including Sections 1–7, every proof in Appendix A.1–A.15, computational tables and references; rendered PDF pages 6, 8, 14, 16, 22, 23 to inspect key formulas

topic_relevance.A01: direct: develops exact projective convex-hull correspondences and finite relaxations for single and multiple fractional objectives, subject to positivity/boundedness conditions.

definitions.name: projective transformation Φ
definitions.statement: For (ρ,x) with ρ>0, Φ(ρ,x)=(1/ρ,x/ρ). It swaps two cross-sections of the same homogenized cone.

definitions.name: fractional image set G
definitions.statement: Given base functions f:X→R^m and α∈R^m, F={f(x):x∈X} and G={f(x)/(αᵀf(x)):x∈X}, where the denominator is positive.

definitions.name: Boolean quadric polytope (BQP)
definitions.statement: For a graph G=(V,E), QP_G=conv{(x,z): x∈{0,1}^{|V|}, z_ij=x_i x_j for (i,j)∈E}. It links 0–1 fractional variables to quadratic monomials.

definitions.name: moment hull
definitions.statement: The convex hull of the univariate moment curve (1,x,…,x^d) over a support interval; the paper obtains reciprocal-function hulls through a projective mapping to this curve.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 1 (convex hull under projective transform)
theorem_cards.statement: conv(S)={(ρ,x):(1,x)∈ρ conv(Φ(S)), ρ>0}, and conversely conv(Φ(S))={(σ,y):(1,y)∈σ conv(S), σ>0}.
proof_steps: The map Φ is an involution, so it is enough to prove one direction.
For a point in the transformed convex hull, express it using convex multipliers λ_j on Φ(ρ_j,x_j).
Reweight by ρλ_j/ρ_j; positivity of every ρ_j makes these nonnegative and their sum is 1, giving a convex combination in S.
For the reverse inclusion, each original point maps into Φ(S), and the constructed set is convex as a cone slice/projection.
gaps: The strict half-space ρ>0 is essential; zero-scale recession points are excluded from the exact non-closed hull formula.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2 (fractional functions and base-image hulls)
assumptions: F and G are the sets defined from common base functions f_i and denominator αᵀf
There exists ε>0 with αᵀf(x)>ε for every x∈X
F is bounded for the first equality
For the reverse equality (7b), additionally f_1(x)=1
theorem_cards.statement: The convex hull of G is obtained by scaling conv(F) and intersecting with αᵀg=1; under f_1=1 the reverse hull relation also holds. A closure version uses the recession cone of cl conv(F).
proof_steps: Lift both sets by adding the denominator coordinate to S and apply Theorem 1.
Project the transform hull to obtain the scaling-and-normalization description.
Boundedness rules out nonzero zero-scale recession vectors satisfying αᵀg=1.
For the reverse formula, f_1=1 makes the first transformed coordinate recover the scale; boundedness closes the zero-scale case.
gaps: Without boundedness, Example 1 shows the exact hull formula can add spurious points; the closure formula needs recession directions explicitly.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition 1 (k-term 0–1 fractional relaxations)
theorem_cards.statement: The k-term relaxation is represented by a homogenized k-th RLT relaxation of the BQP variables with a_0ρ+aᵀy=1. The n-term level yields the exact simultaneous hull in Theorem 3.
proof_steps: Map each ratio subset to a graph-specific BQP through Theorem 2.
Use the affine-independence decomposition lemma for the two-term case.
For higher k, introduce RLT variables so the component lifts share common binary monomials.
gaps: The general BQP hull may be exponentially complex; intermediate levels are relaxations, not exact hulls.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition 2 (bilinear fractional box problem and BQP)
assumptions: Numerator/denominator are bilinear polynomials over the box
theorem_cards.statement: The convex hull of the fractional lift G_G equals {(ρ,y,w):(y,w)∈ρ QP_G, ρ≥0, denominator-normalization=1}; the reverse hull identity also holds. This implies an optimizer exists at a binary vertex for the stated bilinear-ratio class.
proof_steps: Linearize each bilinear term x_i x_j with BQP variables.
Apply Theorem 2 to the positive denominator q_G.
A linear objective over the resulting convex hull attains its optimum at an extreme point corresponding to a BQP vertex.
gaps: Polynomial-time solvability follows only for graph classes with tractable BQP separation, such as the stated series-parallel case.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition 3 (quadratic ratio to quadratic graph hull)
theorem_cards.statement: The hull of the normalized quadratic lift is obtained by scaling conv{(x,xxᵀ):x∈X}, imposing denominator normalization and the lifted affine-face equation. For X=R_+^n this yields an exact completely positive formulation.
proof_steps: First use Theorem 2 without the affine restriction.
Represent L by the valid nonnegative quadratic expression ||Cx−d||²=0.
Intersect with its supporting hyperplane; the cited face-intersection lemma preserves convexification.
Specialize the quadratic hull to the completely positive cone for nonnegative orthant X.
gaps: Exact completely positive optimization is generally hard; the paper’s SDP variant is exact only in the separately stated ball setting or as a relaxation.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 3 (finite hierarchy for multiple ratios)
assumptions: Every denominator a_i0+a_iᵀx is positive on X
theorem_cards.statement: The projected hierarchy is nested, proj_{ρ,y}(R_1)⊇…⊇proj_{ρ,y}(R_n)=conv(G); level n is exact for the simultaneous hull of all ratios.
proof_steps: Lift all ratios with shared monomial variables u.
At each level k, relax each ratio-specific projection with the same k-th RLT variables.
At level n, RLT_n describes the finite binary monomial hull.
The affine-independence decomposition lemma combines the individual lifts into the simultaneous hull.
gaps: Exactness is finite but level-n formulation may be exponentially large; no general polynomial-time claim is made.

constant_dependence.explicit: The projective hull identities depend on a uniform denominator margin ε>0 and bounded F. The multiple-ratio RLT hierarchy is exact at k=n; intermediate levels give nested outer relaxations. BQP optimization is polynomial for the stated series-parallel graph case.
constant_dependence.dependence: RLT/BQP size grows with n and hierarchy level; CP cone formulations are exact representations but can be computationally intractable. Numerical performance statements (gap closed, runtime) are instance- and solver-dependent.

endpoint_limits.denominator: Strict positive denominator is required on the entire feasible set; Theorem 2 strengthens this to a uniform ε>0.
endpoint_limits.boundedness: Bounded F is needed to exclude nonzero recession points from the exact projective hull relation; without it use the explicit closure/recession formula.
endpoint_limits.binary: The finite exact hierarchy assumes a binary domain with shared monomial lifts; continuous-variable variants require their own convexification.
endpoint_limits.graph: BQP relaxations are exact/polynomial only for special graph structures; arbitrary BQP hulls can be NP-hard to separate.
endpoint_limits.quadratic: Quadratic-ratio CP representation assumes bounded domain, positive denominator, and correct affine-face restriction; copositive/CP hardness remains.

reusable_methods.method: Projective convexification via homogenize then renormalize
reusable_methods.transfer: For a common denominator that is uniformly positive, replace the fractional image by a linear slice of the base-function convex hull. Preserve all shared inputs and shared constraints in the lifted object; independent per-event hulls can be strictly weaker, as Example 4 demonstrates.

reusable_methods.method: BQP/RLT lift for finite binary ratios
reusable_methods.transfer: Useful for discretized selection of scales, centers, or source labels with affine ratios; add one common set of binary monomials across all ratios to retain shared-choice coupling.

reusable_methods.method: Copositive/completely positive formulation for quadratic ratios
reusable_methods.transfer: An exact modeling identity for nonnegative quadratic variables under positive denominator; using an SDP/DNN approximation requires separate containment and gap justification.
Map reciprocal terms with poles outside the support interval to a polynomial moment curve when denominator signs are fixed over the domain.

unchecked: Full paper and every Appendix A proof were read. I independently checked that Φ is an involution, verified the convex-combination reweighting in Theorem 1, and checked the role of positivity and boundedness in Theorem 2. I did not independently rederive every BQP/RLT and completely-positive cone characterization, reproduce the numerical experiments, or validate solver tolerances; those portions remain author-reported or depend on cited polyhedral/moment results. The paper supplies a counterexample to the weaker strategy that convexifies each ratio separately, which is relevant to preserving joint choices.
